The public regression tests pass (124 tests, OK). My edit is in place in the allowed file `django/db/models/sql/query.py`.

The fix detects when aggregates reference annotations containing window functions (`contains_over_clause`) and forces the subquery path, so the window function is computed in the inner query rather than being nested inside an aggregate in the outer query — resolving the `GroupingError: aggregate function calls cannot contain window function calls`.

action.message:
Implemented the fix in django/db/models/sql/query.py (the only allowed file).

Problem: Since Django 4.2, calling `.aggregate()` on a queryset whose annotations contain Window functions produced SQL nesting a window function inside an aggregate (e.g. `SUM(COALESCE(SUM(...) OVER (...), 0.0))`), which PostgreSQL rejects with `GroupingError: aggregate function calls cannot contain window function calls`.

Change: In `Query.get_aggregation()`, added a `refs_window` check that inspects the refs of the resolved aggregates and detects when any referenced annotation has `contains_over_clause` (i.e. contains a window function). This flag is added to the condition that decides whether to wrap the query in a subquery, so window-function annotations are computed in the inner query and the outer aggregate operates on the resulting column instead of inlining the window function.

Verification: scoped_tests public regression selection ("aggregation") passed — 124 tests, OK, returncode 0.
